## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}

packages <- c("tidyverse", "readxl", "readr", "data.table", "dplyr", "stringr", "ggplot2", "sf", "fs", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata", "rio", "countrycode","maps", "stringi","rnaturalearthdata","devtools", "pack", "cli", "remotes", "countrycode","progress", "tidygeocoder", "dplyr", "readr", "purrr","ggplot","qs2" )

# Install packages not yet installed [for the first time]
installed_packages <- packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(installed_packages == FALSE)) {
 install.packages(packages[!installed_packages])
}

# Packages loading
invisible(lapply(packages, require, character.only = TRUE)) # remove "invisible" to see whether the packages are loaded/available. 

Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "Spanish_Spain.1252") # en Windows


```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}

dfCR <- read.csv2("./data/Georreferencing/1.Raw/georef__CR2024.csv",sep = ",")

names(df) # check names of the columns
View(df) # if you want to open and see the file
str(dfCR) #solo
head(dfCR) # if you want to see more or less the structure of the dataframe (df)



```

```{r}
dfAmaz <- df %>%
  filter(.ok_for_analysis == FALSE,
         !is.na(decimalLatitude),
         !is.na(decimalLongitude)) %>%
  select(
    occurrenceID,
    decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude,
    locality, country, countryCode,
    changes
  )

View(dfAmaz)


dfCR1 <- dfCR %>%
  filter(.ok_for_analysis == FALSE,
         !is.na(decimalLatitude),
         !is.na(decimalLongitude)) %>%
  select(
    occurrenceID,
    decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude,
    locality, country, countryCode,
    changes
  )

View(dfCR1)


dfcrd <- dfCR %>%
  mutate(
    georef_class = case_when(
      is.na(locality) | str_squish(locality) == "" ~ "non_georef",
      str_detect(locality, regex(
        "\\d+\\s*km|carretera|road|highway|reserva|parque nacional|río|quebrada|cerro|vereda",
        ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "detailed",
      TRUE ~ "simple"
    )
  )

view(dfcrd)
```

```{r}
plot(dfAmaz$decimalLongitude, dfAmaz$decimalLatitude,
     xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",
     main = "Decimal Coordinates",
     pch = 19, col = "blue")


# Get world map data
world <- map_data("world")

# Filter for selected countries
countries <- c("Peru", "Brazil", "Ecuador", "Colombia")
region_map <- subset(world, region %in% countries)

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = region_map,
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = region),
               color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = df, aes(x = decimalLongitude, y = decimalLatitude),
             color = "red", size = 3) +
  coord_fixed(1.3, xlim = c(-82, -45), ylim = c(-20, 10)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Peru" = "lightblue",
                               "Brazil" = "lightgreen",
                               "Ecuador" = "orange",
                               "Colombia" = "pink")) +
  labs(title = "Selected Countries with Coordinates",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", fill = "Country")
```

#Database supervition AMAZ

```{r}
#AMAZ2024

AMAZ <- read.csv2("./data/Georreferencing/2.Processed/georef__AMAZ2024.csv",sep = ",")
#view(AMAZ)
unique(AMAZ$stateProvince)
unique(AMAZ$country)

# Diccionario de provincias -> departamentos
province_to_dep <- c(
  "Maynas" = "Loreto",
  "Oxapampa" = "Pasco",
  "Bagua" = "Amazonas",
  "Loreto" = "Loreto",
  "Requena" = "Loreto",
  "Tarma" = "Junín",
  "Alto Amazonas" = "Loreto",
  "Mariscal Caceres" = "San Martin",
  "Chanchamayo" = "Junin",
  "Ramon Castilla" = "Loreto",
  "Tambopata" = "Madre de Dios",
  "Ucayali" = "Loreto",  # Provincia de Ucayali está en Loreto
  "Coronel Portillo" = "Ucayali",
  "Coronel portillo" = "Ucayali",
  "Morona" = "Loreto",
  "San Ignacio" = "Cajamarca",
  "Tamshiyacu" = "Loreto",
  "Luya" = "Amazonas",
  "Leoncio Prado" = "Huanuco",
  "Jenaro Herrera" = "Loreto",
  "Rioja" = "San Martin"
)

# Aplicar la corrección directamente a stateProvince
AMAZ$stateProvince <- province_to_dep[AMAZ$stateProvince]

# Verificar el resultado
unique(AMAZ$stateProvince)


#AMAZ_199=Madre de Dios
#AMAZ_200=Madre de Dios
#AMAZ_208=Loreto
#AMAZ_222=Ucayali
#AMAZ_231= Country=Ecuador, countryCode=EC, stateProvince=Napo
#AMAZ_369=Junin

# Diccionario de occurrenceID -> ubicación
location_mapping <- list(
  "AMAZ_199" = list(
    country = "Peru",
    countryCode = "PE",
    stateProvince = "Madre de Dios"
  ),
  "AMAZ_200" = list(
    country = "Peru",
    countryCode = "PE",
    stateProvince = "Madre de Dios"
  ),
  "AMAZ_208" = list(
    country = "Peru",
    countryCode = "PE",
    stateProvince = "Loreto"  # Iquitos está en Loreto
  ),
  "AMAZ_222" = list(
    country = "Peru",
    countryCode = "PE",
    stateProvince = "Ucayali"
  ),
  "AMAZ_231" = list(
    country = "Ecuador",
    countryCode = "EC",
    stateProvince = "Napo"
  ),
  "AMAZ_369" = list(
    country = "Peru",
    countryCode = "PE",
    stateProvince = "Junín"
  ),
  "AMAZ_74" = list(
    country = "Peru",
    countryCode = "PE",
    stateProvince = "San Martin"
))

# Aplicar las asignaciones
for(id in names(location_mapping)) {
  # Filtrar las filas que coinciden con el occurrenceID
  rows <- which(AMAZ$occurrenceID == id)
  
  if(length(rows) > 0) {
    # Asignar los valores
    AMAZ$country[rows] <- location_mapping[[id]]$country
    AMAZ$countryCode[rows] <- location_mapping[[id]]$countryCode
    AMAZ$stateProvince[rows] <- location_mapping[[id]]$stateProvince
  }
}

# Verificar los cambios
AMAZ[AMAZ$occurrenceID %in% names(location_mapping), 
     c("occurrenceID", "country", "countryCode", "stateProvince")]


write.csv(AMAZ, file = "data/Georreferencing/2.Processed/georef__AMAZ2024.csv")


```

```{r}
  CR$stateProvince %in% names(state_corrections),
  state_corrections[CR$stateProvince],
  CR$stateProvince
)

# 3. Convertir valores vacíos a NA
CR$stateProvince <- ifelse(CR$stateProvince == "", NA_character_, CR$stateProvince)

# 4. Corregir países incorrectos (sin tildes)
CR$country <- case_when(
  # Rio San Juan es Nicaragua, no Costa Rica
  CR$country == "Costa Rica" & CR$stateProvince == "Rio San Juan" ~ "Nicaragua",
  # Bluefields es Nicaragua
  CR$country == "Belize" & CR$stateProvince == "Bluefields" ~ "Nicaragua",
  # San Blas es Panama
  CR$country == "Panama" & CR$stateProvince == "San Blas" ~ "Panama",
  # Por defecto mantener el país original
  TRUE ~ CR$country
)

# 5. Verificar resultado
resultado_final <- CR %>%
```
